# Replacing bulb in heater unit on Peugeot 207

Replacing the dashboard light on a Peugeot 207 is a classic automotive engineering puzzle that often trips up DIYers because the assembly design prioritizes structural rigidity over serviceability. You have correctly identified the first two steps: removing the two silver trim strips from the center console and unscrewing the heater panel to release its front clip. However, your current impasseâthe inability to slide the unit out once the clips are freeâis a known characteristic of this specific vehicle platform.

The core issue lies in the mounting mechanism. On the Peugeot 207, the heater control unit is not simply a drawer that slides out; it is mechanically keyed into the dashboard cavity. When you push the panel "in and down" to disengage the front clips, you have successfully released the front retention points, but the rear of the unit remains seated against the firewall or the instrument cluster housing. The cable harnesses are also routed in a way that prevents the unit from being pulled backward without significant maneuvering.

To proceed, you must access the underside of the dashboard, which is far less elegant than the top-down approach but technically necessary. Before attempting to force the unit out, you need to disconnect the electrical connectors. Locate the main power harness and the specific connector for the bulb (usually a simple two-pin or three-pin plug). If the connector is tight, apply gentle leverage; do not yank the wires, as this can snap the internal pins or damage the loom insulation. Once disconnected, you will have some slack in the wiring that allows for movement.

The next critical step involves removing the rear retaining screws. These are typically Torx bolts (often T20 or T25) located behind the glove box or accessible through the kick panel area near the driver's door hinge. You may need to remove the glove box entirely if the screws are hidden behind it. This is a common oversight in online forums; the screws are not always visible from the top of the console. Once these rear fasteners are removed, the unit is no longer structurally bound to the chassis.

With the electrical connections severed and the rear mounting points cleared, you can now carefully maneuver the heater unit forward and upward. The design requires you to tilt the entire assembly slightly forward to clear the dashboard bulkhead before sliding it out completely. This motion releases the side clips that were previously hidden by the console depth. Be cautious during this extraction: the bulb housing is fragile, and the internal wiring loom can be brittle with age. If the unit resists movement, stop immediately. Forcing it risks breaking the plastic tabs on the unit itself, which would require a complete replacement of the heater assembly rather than just the bulb.

Once the unit is free from the dashboard cavity, you will have access to the bulb socket. On many Peugeot 207 models, the bulb is held in place by a simple twist-lock mechanism or a retaining clip accessible from the front once the casing is removed. Identify the correct bulb type (commonly an incandescent T10 or LED equivalent depending on your specific trim level and market year) and swap it out.

After replacement, reverse the installation process. Reconnect all electrical harnesses securely, ensuring no pins are loose. Insert the heater unit back into the cavity, aligning the side clips and rear mounting points. Tighten the rear screws first to stabilize the unit, then push it forward until the front clips snap into place with an audible click. Replace the silver trim strips on the center console.

If you encounter resistance at any stage where the unit will not slide out after disconnecting the cables and removing rear screws, inspect for broken plastic tabs or debris in the mounting cavity that might be catching on the dashboard edge. In such cases, professional assistance may be required to avoid damaging the dashboard structure permanently.
